leading_positions.synthesis: Four members put the optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) as their preferred single-part prize, and all four word the citation around the magic-wavelength lattice clock reaching about 1e-18. Shared: the two-name attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist, and independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE) reproduce and compare the clocks. Not shared: whether this is a distinct discovery or an extension of the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, how much weight a precision-measurement result deserves against a discovery about nature, and how much of Ye's contribution lies in already-recognised laser stabilisation and comb work. Two of the four (Pearce, Kroll) arrived at this position after hearing colleagues; Pearce moved up from sixth in the opening ranking, and the Chair's own earlier first choice (B010) has no other supporter.

Four members prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) as a single-part prize, framed as a 2011 prediction followed by the 2018 experiments, reproduced by many groups and spreading across van der Waals materials. Shared: the citation should rest on flat bands and the correlated insulating and superconducting states, not on a pairing mechanism, and the Bistritzer-MacDonald pair should not be split. Not shared: how much the open pairing mechanism and twist-angle disorder count against maturity, and how seriously to take the earlier flat-band work and the uncredited experimental co-first authors. Danielsson and Mehlig moved to this position from other first choices (B047 and B011) after reading the opening ballots.

areas_of_agreement: The eight explicit preferred configurations split evenly: four for B049 and four for B009, each as a single-part prize with its supplied laureate names; no member prefers a two-part prize in round 1.

Both leading candidates have settled laureate lists as proposed: all eight members' preferred configurations use exactly the credited names for B049 (Katori, Ye) and for B009 (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer), and every B009 supporter would keep Bistritzer.

Each leading candidate is named as an explicit alternative by supporters of the other: Johansson, Kroll and Lindroth list B009 as an alternative to B049, and Pearce does the same, while Danielsson, Eriksson and Olsson list B049 as an alternative to B009 (Eriksson and Danielsson alongside other candidates). Mehlig, a B009 supporter, lists B012 and B011 instead.

Several members state that the citation should be narrow and phenomenon-specific: the magic-wavelength lattice clock for B049, and flat bands plus correlated states (not the pairing mechanism) for B009.

Every member who addresses B047 (IceCube) agrees that the science is real but that a Halzen-only prize does not represent AMANDA, Baikal, DUMAND or the collaboration, and that source identification is still modest. Danielsson, its first-ranking proponent, has moved it to an alternative.
scientific_disputes: Whether the lattice clock is a new discovery (many-atom, Doppler- and recoil-free interrogation giving a statistical-stability gain over single ions) or a very large refinement of an honoured measurement lineage, as Danielsson, Olsson and Eriksson question it and Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce list it as their own main reservation.

Whether a measurement-precision result should weigh below a discovery from nature; Danielsson and Eriksson say they have not yet seen a new physical phenomenon from the clocks, while their supporters point to millimetre-scale redshift tests and constraints on constants already in hand.

Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism in twisted bilayer graphene makes the discovery premature, or whether the reproduced phase diagram is sufficient; Johansson and Olsson (in her statement of reservation) and Mehlig flag the issue, Eriksson and Danielsson argue it is the normal state of a young field.

Whether active-matter hydrodynamics (B011, Mehlig's alternative) has decisive experimental confirmation of the Toner-Tu predictions; Pearce and Johansson note only partial tests and no other member ranks it.
attribution_disputes: B009: earlier flat-band work by Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, the experimental co-first authors (Cao, Fatemi) and Cory Dean's group are outside the credited names; members disagree whether the Bistritzer-MacDonald quantitative magic-angle prediction is the decisive prior contribution.

B049: whether Lemonde (SYRTE), Hollberg, Gill, NIST colleagues and the single-ion clock community have a claim that makes a two-person prize incomplete, and how Ye's comb and stabilisation work should be treated in the citation.

B012 (an alternative for Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson): opening proposals differ between Greiner and Cirac alongside Bloch and Zoller; Jaksch is not credited; Lindroth, Kroll and Johansson favour Bloch, Greiner and Zoller, while Mehlig, who opened with Cirac, concedes that omitting Greiner is a real cost.
B047: a single credited name (Halzen) for a detector and collaboration built by many; B010: the role of the late Jan van Paradijs and the division of credit between BeppoSAX and follow-up groups.
maturity_disputes: B009: whether to recognise now or wait, given the unsettled pairing mechanism, twist-angle disorder and the possibility that the fractional Chern insulator gives a more stable later result; Danielsson and Olsson answer in their responses that the fractional Chern insulator argues for a later prize, not for withholding this one.
B049: the redefinition of the second has not yet happened, so the practical payoff is prospective; Johansson, Kroll and Pearce each state that the physics is confirmed regardless of the redefinition.
B047 and B029: source identification for IceCube rests on one blazar coincidence and a Galactic-plane map, and Danielsson and the Chair view the nanohertz gravitational-wave background as premature.

B040: circuit QED is scientifically strong, but Johansson (who moved it down from his opening rank 2) and Lindroth (who ranked it 8th) cite the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits as making another award in that area hard so soon.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (Chalmers, WACQT director) discloses closeness to the B040 groups (Wallraff, Schoelkopf, Blais) and says he should recuse from any decision on B040.

Kroll discloses a year in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder during his PhD, in the JILA group where Jun Ye (credited on B049) works, with no known current collaboration; he suggests the committee note it.

Mehlig discloses an intellectual bias toward B011 (active matter) from his own machine-learning work, stated as a bias and not a recusal; he also shares the Gothenburg environment with Johansson and Olsson, with no specific collaboration.

Pearce (Chair) works in the PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations, adjacent to B010 and B047, and opened by ranking B010 first; no tie to any credited person identified, and neither is part of his preferred configuration.

Olsson notes Chalmers colleagues in Johansson and the neighbouring GU department of Mehlig, and that Chalmers has superconducting-circuit activity relevant to B040, which she does not prefer; Lindroth discloses long-time collaboration with a 2023 laureate (Anne L'Huillier) but none of the credited names on B049, B012 or B009.
questions_for_round2: B049 versus B009: is the committee prepared to choose between a cleanly attributed, mature precision measurement and a prediction-plus-discovery whose pairing mechanism is open, and what additional evidence would move either side?

Lattice clock: what precisely is new relative to the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, and can a citation be written around the magic-wavelength lattice so that Ye's comb and stabilisation work and the single-ion lineage do not need to be resolved?
Lattice clock: does the record on Lemonde, Hollberg, Gill and NIST colleagues support a two-person B049 prize, and who first demonstrated the lattice clock?

Twisted bilayer graphene: which parts of the 2018 discovery are settled enough to cite without a pairing mechanism, and does the primary literature support crediting Bistritzer-MacDonald over Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto for the magic-angle prediction?

Twisted bilayer graphene: can the committee defend omitting Cao, Fatemi and other co-first authors and Cory Dean's group within a three-name limit, or does that attribution gap argue for a different candidate or postponement?

Is a two-part prize possible given that B049 uses two names and B009 uses three, and if so would any member explicitly support a combined configuration, or should round 2 treat each as a competing single-part option?

B012 and B047: if either is to remain an alternative, can the committee settle the three-name allocation (Greiner versus Cirac, Jaksch) for B012, and name a defensible second and third laureate for B047 beyond Halzen?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows two positions with equal explicit support, B049 with four members and B009 with four, each a single-part prize with agreed names; no other ballot has a preferred-configuration supporter. The disagreement is mainly about maturity and novelty (lineage for the clock, an open mechanism for the graphene) and about attribution, not the quality of the science. The Chair, who opened with B010 first, now prefers B049 largely on the judgment of atomic-physics colleagues and treats that as a limit on his own confidence; round 2 should rely on the primary-literature checks requested above.
